title.en: Compute net profit before tax from Balance Sheet data

say.en: Start with the profit figure and undo everything that was not cash: depreciation, gains on sale, and money stuck in stock and debtors. What remains is operating cash. In this lesson: Compute net profit before tax from Balance Sheet data.
Make non-cash and non-operating adjustments.
Adjust working capital changes.

body.en: Net *profit* before tax = closing surplus − opening surplus + transfers to reserves + interim dividend paid + provision for tax made during the year. Add non-cash and non-operating charges: depreciation, amortisation (goodwill, patents written off), loss on sale of assets, finance costs (interest on debentures and loans). Deduct non-operating incomes: profit on sale of assets, interest and dividend received. Result: operating profit before working capital changes.

problem.en: Surplus rose from ₹1,00,000 to ₹2,50,000; ₹50,000 transferred to General Reserve; provision for tax made ₹80,000; depreciation ₹50,000; loss on sale of machinery ₹10,000; interest on debentures ₹30,000; dividend received ₹20,000; inventories up ₹30,000; trade receivables down ₹20,000; trade payables up ₹15,000; outstanding expenses down ₹5,000; tax paid ₹70,000. Find net cash from operating activities.

steps.en: Working capital: − 30,000 + 20,000 + 15,000 − 5,000 = 0; cash generated from operations = ₹3,50,000.
Less tax paid ₹70,000: net cash from operating activities = ₹2,80,000.

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. Surplus rose from 1,00,000 rupees to 2,50,000 rupees; 50,000 rupees transferred to General Reserve; provision for tax made 80,000 rupees; depreciation 50,000 rupees; loss on sale of machinery 10,000 rupees; interest on debentures 30,000 rupees; dividend received 20,000 rupees; inventories up 30,000 rupees; trade receivables down 20,000 rupees; trade payables up 15,000 rupees; outstanding expenses down 5,000 rupees; tax paid 70,000 rupees. Find net cash from operating activities.
Net profit before tax equals 1,50,000 plus 50,000 plus 80,000 equals 2,80,000 rupees.
Operating profit before WC changes equals 2,80,000 plus 50,000 plus 10,000 plus 30,000 minus 20,000 equals 3,50,000 rupees.
Working capital: minus 30,000 plus 20,000 plus 15,000 minus 5,000 equals 0; cash generated from operations equals 3,50,000 rupees.
Less tax paid 70,000 rupees: net cash from operating activities equals 2,80,000 rupees.
So the answer is 2,80,000 rupees.
